key_insight: The paper argues that robots learn task steps and object roles—not just visual appearances—from in-context examples. This semantic knowledge could help manipulation skills transfer across scenes, provided learning accounts for the robot’s current world.
problem_solved: Trained robot policies are tied to their training distributions, while demonstrations from other scenes lack feedback from the environment the robot currently faces, limiting in-context learning.
method: Use in-context experience to convey manipulation knowledge rather than relying solely on skills encoded in trained network weights.
Focus on semantic task structure, including action steps and object roles, as transferable knowledge across environments.
Frame current-world feedback as a missing ingredient; the provided abstract is truncated and does not specify the full mechanism.
impact: This direction could make robot skills more reusable across changing environments without retraining for every scene. The supplied excerpt does not include results establishing performance gains.
visual_elements: Side-by-side diagram: skills stored in network weights versus task knowledge supplied in context.

Robot–environment feedback loop highlighting information absent from an external demonstration.
Task storyboard with role labels such as target object and destination.
paper_title: World In-Context Learning for Agentic Robot Manipulation
paper_authors: Heng Fang, Zehui Guo, Yuehan Zhang, Mingyang Du, Dingkang Liang
